EnrolmentsService is an application-layer service, so its job is to orchestrate use cases: load aggregates, call domain behaviour and persist the results. Most of the file does that. Course.admit() and Enrolment.withinCoolingOff() are delegated to the domain correctly. However, the file also does work that belongs to other layers.

1. Persistence mapping (infrastructure): the service works directly with TypeORM Repository<EnrolmentEntity> and Repository<CourseEntity>. It writes the query shapes itself (findOne/count/delete with `where` clauses). It also maps between ORM rows and domain objects by hand: toCourse(entity), `entity.enrolled = course.enrolled`, `this.enrolmentRepository.create({ ...enrolment })`, and `new Enrolment(row.courseId, row.studentEmail, row.enrolledAt)`. Mapping rows to domain objects and back is the job of a repository or adapter in the infrastructure layer.

2. A domain rule in the application layer: enrol() checks whether the student email is valid (`!studentEmail.includes('@')`) and throws DomainError('invalid'). This is a rule of the Enrolment domain object, so it belongs in the domain layer, not in the application service.

Using repositories from an application service is common in NestJS, so confidence is moderate. Still, the hand-written row mapping and the inline domain rule are responsibilities of other layers.
